variants.title: Strain gauge on a steel cantilever: half bridge
variants.sample: Steel cantilever, tension and compression gauges in a half bridge
variants.unknown: the strain and an unknown weight with a half bridge
variants.note: With a gauge on the top face (tension) and one on the bottom (compression) the bridge output is twice that of a single gauge, and the temperature effects cancel.

source.title: Strain gauge bridge configurations: Hoffmann, An Introduction to Measurements using Strain Gauges (HBM)

variants.title: Strain gauge on a steel cantilever: full bridge
variants.sample: Steel cantilever, four gauges in a full bridge
variants.unknown: the strain and an unknown weight with a full bridge
variants.note: Four active gauges give four times the single-gauge output and cancel temperature drift, which is why load cells use them.

source.title: Strain gauge bridge configurations: Hoffmann, An Introduction to Measurements using Strain Gauges (HBM)

variants.title: Strain gauge on an aluminium cantilever: quarter bridge
variants.sample: Aluminium 6061-T6 cantilever, E = 68.9 GPa, quarter bridge
variants.unknown: the strain and an unknown weight on a softer beam
variants.note: Aluminium is about three times less stiff than steel, so the same load gives about three times the strain and output.

source.title: Young's modulus of aluminium alloy 6061-T6: 68.9 GPa (MatWeb / ASM handbook value)
